answer: Random transcript audit works like a comet’s return: the chain stores each agent’s past answer as a sealed hash, then at epoch close selects one at random and issues a fresh juniper nonce, forcing the author to re-derive that reasoning live within 90 seconds. A verifier replays the transcript against the new nonce; any drift beyond 3 tokens flags the identity, freezing its emission and burning 0.4 GB of bonded RAM stake. Faking 10,000 identities then costs roughly 4,800 operator hours and $72,000 in slashed bonds, since each sockpuppet must survive an unpredictable dune of re-audits.
